homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym of the name: the four cards concern the organisation (B1), its foundation (B2, B3) and Uber's share of fares (B4, a video whose title does not name the entity). 'WIE' is the entity's acronym, used by its own pages (B3) and the census (aka). The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the organisation and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: Stichting WIE International (workerinfoexchange.nl), the Dutch foundation 'working in cooperation with Worker Info Exchange' (B2 F26): a distinct body, which the census lists among the entity's names (aka) and the composition merges into it (CAP-1-02)
the Dynamic Pay Claim and its campaign site dynamicpay.org (the action and its campaign, linked from both sites)
Uber (the platform the action is brought against)
the TUC and its report The Human Price of Dynamic Pay (B3)
the University of Oxford (the joint audit, B2, B3)
the International Alliance of App-based Transport Workers and the App Drivers and Couriers Union (Wikipedia's one mention, B6)
NOVO ORG (the video card's poster, B4)

the census's neighbours in its worked question on automated management: coworker-bossware-database and ilo-platform-policy-tracker (no /non rows at datasets/negative-of-the-negative/v2/rows/ for them when this row was built; none edited)

captures.description: WORKER INFO EXCHANGE, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a non-profit organization based in London (operating also as Stichting WIE International) that fights for the digital and labor rights of gig economy workers.' Data control through subject access requests, algorithmic accountability, collective legal action against Uber's dynamic pay, research with the University of Oxford and the TUC. Four cards: its own site, two Stichting WIE International pages, a Facebook video.

atoms.evidence: Helps gig workers use data access and Subject Access Requests (SARs) to see how tech platforms track pay, work allocation, and performance.
